title: Error Handling Layer Architecture
purpose: Show the 5-layer error handling pipeline from backend async route handler wrapping through AppError classes, error handler middleware, Axios response interceptor, and the missing React ErrorBoundary.
audience: Backend and frontend developers, QA engineers, architects
description: Five-layer error handling pipeline: Layer 1 (asyncHandler wrapper in utils/asyncHandler.ts) catches unhandled promise rejections in route handlers and passes to next(err). Layer 2 (AppError classes in utils/apiError.ts) with subtypes: NotFoundError, BadRequestError, UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError — two identical AppError classes exist in different locations (duplication). Layer 3 (Error Handler Middleware in middleware/error.middleware.ts) is the global catch-all via app.use(err, req, res, next), prunes stack trace in production, returns structured JSON { success: false, error: { message, statusCode } }, and converts unknown errors to generic Internal server error. Layer 4 (Axios Response Interceptor in apiClient.ts) catches HTTP errors on frontend, auto-clears auth token on 401 and redirects to login, shows toast notification for other errors, no retry logic except where 5xx configured. Layer 5 (React ErrorBoundary) is MISSING — no ErrorBoundary component exists, uncaught React errors crash the UI.

All operational errors should use AppError subtypes
Error middleware must be registered after all routes

Missing ErrorBoundary means the entire UI is vulnerable to crashes
